open_questions.question: Is a refund on day 30 after purchase allowed (inclusive) or blocked (exclusive)? Are days counted as calendar days in the store's local time?
Does the POS ever prompt for or accept a card at refund time, or does it always route to the original tender automatically? What should happen if a different card is presented?
How does the tester create sales with past purchase dates (2026-09-17, 2026-10-01 to 2026-10-22) in the test environment? Can sale dates be backdated or the register clock changed?

For partial refunds on split-tender sales, is the last-paid tender refunded up to its paid amount before any earlier tender? How can a tester observe the refund order (POS screen order, SAP timestamps, other)?
Are partial refunds line-item only, or can a cashier enter an arbitrary amount? Can a line with qty > 1 be partly refunded?
Does 'over $500' mean strictly greater than $500.00? Is the threshold compared to this refund's amount, the cumulative refunds on the sale, or the sale total? Is tax included?
What happens when the manager rejects the approval or the prompt is cancelled: is the refund cancelled, and can the cashier retry on the same sale?
Is store credit issued for the full amount owed to the expired/closed card? In what form (card number, voucher ID) and how is it verified? How is a sale paid by MC_EXPIRED or AMEX_CLOSED set up?
For a split-tender refund, does POS send one SAP message per tender or one message covering all tenders?
What events start and end the 5-minute window (refund confirmation to SAP receipt?), and do retries under R8 have to finish within the same 5 minutes? What is the retry interval?
What are the expected formats of tenderType (card brand, test card name, code) and timestamp (format, time zone)?
Does 'retries 3 times' mean 4 total attempts? Does the SAP stub or the Integration log record each failed attempt so the tester can count them? What fields does the error log entry contain?
Does the customer's refund still complete when all SAP sends fail, and is anything shown to the cashier?

coverage_notes: R3 has no standalone negative test: the only failure mode is refunding in the wrong order, which is checked as an expected result in TC-008, TC-010, TC-021 and TC-026. There is no invalid input for R3 to reject.

R7 5-minute boundary: the test environment gives no way to make POS send at exactly 4:59, 5:00 or 5:01. TC-028 checks the inbox at those three points and measures the actual delay; a send later than 5:00 can be observed but not induced.
R8 boundary uses the SAP stub fail-next-N setting: N=2 (below), N=3 (at, success on the last retry), N=4 (above, all attempts fail). TC-032 (N=1) also covers the 'succeeds on retry' scenario.
Transaction IDs (TXN-1001 to TXN-1036) and SKUs (SKU-200 to SKU-506) are setup identifiers the tester creates; <test_env> provides no catalog. Prices were chosen to hit the BRD limits.
Amounts assume no tax because the BRD does not mention tax; see Q-06.
All tests are P1 because every requirement in BRD-POS-017 governs money movement, approvals or SAP data.
The BRD does not define POS screen wording, so screen expectations describe the outcome (completed, blocked, approval prompt) rather than exact text.

Required scenarios: split + partial (TC-009, TC-010), split + approval (TC-021), split + expired card (TC-026), multiple partials reaching total (TC-013), approval rejected (TC-019), same refund twice (TC-014), SAP succeeds on retry (TC-032 to TC-034).
